headline: Maui Planning Commission - Meeting of July 14, 2026

meeting.body: Maui Planning Commission - Meeting of July 14, 2026
meeting.summary: The commission approved restrooms and showers at Mākena State Park, six to one, with a carrying capacity study due by July 31, 2029.
meeting.recap: The commission returned to a State Parks request for restrooms, showers, and parking upgrades at Mākena State Park.[[0:01:36]] Public testimony closed at the June 23 meeting.[[0:02:06]] Commissioners added a condition that the study report is due by July 31, 2029.[[1:59:52]] A State Parks lawyer said resident-only parking would likely be found unconstitutional.[[2:04:23]] The commission approved the permit, six to one.[[2:21:29]] The commission took up its written decision on permits for a solar project.[[2:23:59]] The commission voted to adopt that decision.[[2:27:36]] Planning staff updated the commission on rewriting Title 19, the county zoning code.[[2:30:32]] Staff said the first draft chapters should come later this summer or fall.[[2:48:16]] A consultant said Maui's special management area (SMA), a protected coastal zone, has not changed since 1979.[[3:14:09]] One testifier asked that wheelchair access standards be written into SMA rules.[[3:25:37]] The next meeting is July 28.[[4:06:14]]
decided: The commission adopted the written decision and the motion carried.
meeting.next: State Parks will keep working with the fire department to fix tight spots in the parking lot. Planning staff said they will revise condition 3 to reference the State's July 2 letter. The solar project's state permit moves to the Land Use Commission.
